name: Mospi Legacy Data Extraction Tool
what_it_holds: Hackathon tool ('Mospi Legacy Data Extraction Tool') to extract, digitize, and process historical datasets from India's Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI); includes a user guide in the README. 2 stars, updated Mar 2026.
why_useful: Directly targets the stated gap-7 need for an India MOSPI client, specifically for legacy (pre-digital) datasets that are otherwise hard to access; quality is hackathon-grade so treat as a lead to verify, not a turnkey tool.
themes: Regional macro for LatAm and APAC: Mexico INEGI/Banxico, Brazil IBGE/BCB, Argentina INDEC, Colombia DANE, Chile, Japan e-Stat, Korea KOSIS, Australia ABS, India MOSPI clients
why_all: Directly targets the stated gap-7 need for an India MOSPI client, specifically for legacy (pre-digital) datasets that are otherwise hard to access; quality is hackathon-grade so treat as a lead to verify, not a turnkey tool.

name: webgraph (LAW / vigna)
what_it_holds: The core WebGraph framework (Java) for compressing and analyzing large web graphs and computing rank measures (PageRank, harmonic centrality) — the underlying library that Common Crawl's cc-webgraph and the LAW group's Common Crawl host-rank releases are built on. No data committed, just the compression/ranking library.
why_useful: Foundational dependency for anyone wanting to reproduce or verify Common Crawl host-graph rank numbers rather than a data source itself; low direct value beyond method provenance.
license: unspecified in fetch (check repo, historically LGPL/Apache dual)
themes: Web-traffic estimates and domain ranks: Similarweb scrapers or samples, Cloudflare Radar API, Chrome UX Report popularity rank, Tranco, Majestic Million, Common Crawl host-graph rank
why_all: Foundational dependency for anyone wanting to reproduce or verify Common Crawl host-graph rank numbers rather than a data source itself; low direct value beyond method provenance.

name: influenza-wikipedia-dataset
what_it_holds: Committed dataset (4 stars) pairing influenza incidence surveillance data with Wikipedia pagecounts/pageviews for disease-related articles, built for infodemiology/nowcasting research.
why_useful: Not travel-relevant directly, but it is a concrete, committed example of the exact methodology pattern (pageviews as a leading/coincident indicator for a real-world demand series, validated against ground truth) that the team could replicate for tourism articles — useful as a methods reference for gap #17 (nowcasting with mixed-frequency data) even though the topic is epidemiology.
geography: not specified (likely Italy/EU given fluTN org name)
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Not travel-relevant directly, but it is a concrete, committed example of the exact methodology pattern (pageviews as a leading/coincident indicator for a real-world demand series, validated against ground truth) that the team could replicate for tourism articles — useful as a methods reference for gap #17 (nowcasting with mixed-frequency data) even though the topic is epidemiology.

Off-theme (health, not travel) but a concrete precedent/template repo for 'Wikipedia pageviews of a topic committed alongside a real-world outcome series for nowcasting' - the exact data-shape a tourism-demand version of this project would need to produce; worth knowing as a methods reference rather than a direct data source.

name: pytrends
what_it_holds: The original, most widely used unofficial Python client for Google Trends (interest over time, by region, related topics/queries, realtime/trending searches, top charts). 3.7k stars, 889 forks, 635 commits, 136 open issues. Archived/read-only by the owner on 17 Apr 2025 — no longer maintained.
why_useful: This is almost certainly the tool already behind our '9 terms, NOT point-in-time' Google Trends holding, so it is a duplicate of what we already use operationally rather than a new find — flagged for completeness and because it is the base layer several of the other candidates below (gtab, longtrends, GoogleTrends-Scraper) build on to fix the point-in-time / long-history problems pytrends alone has.
duplicate_of_holding: Google Trends (9 terms) already held per CONTEXT.md — pytrends is presumably the client used to pull it
themes: Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos
why_all: This is almost certainly the tool already behind our '9 terms, NOT point-in-time' Google Trends holding, so it is a duplicate of what we already use operationally rather than a new find — flagged for completeness and because it is the base layer several of the other candidates below (gtab, longtrends, GoogleTrends-Scraper) build on to fix the point-in-time / long-history problems pytrends alone has.

This is almost certainly the tool underlying our existing 9-term Trends pull (already tested and found not to beat naive). Flagging mainly because it is now archived — any new Trends work should move to a maintained fork (trendspyg, pytrends-modern) or the anchored gtab method rather than pytrends itself.

name: google-trends-daily
what_it_holds: GPL-3.0 Python tool (50 stars) to reconstruct daily Google Trends data over extended periods via overlapping-window stitching, one of the earlier/well-known implementations of this pattern.
why_useful: Third independent implementation of the daily-reconstruction pattern; useful as a cross-check against longtrends/GoogleTrends-Scraper outputs for the same keyword set (methodological triangulation on gap #17).
themes: Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos
